title: opum-workflow SessionEnd hook creates a self-sustaining tracker-chore PR loop
summary: The SessionEnd (and PreCompact) hook body in hooks/flush-state.sh always dirties the working tree: step 2 unconditionally rewrites .claude/handovers/cursor.md, and step 1 appends a boilerplate implementation note ('Session <reason> at <ts>. Branch <b>, N uncommitted file(s)...') to the tracker whenever exactly one task is In Progress -- regardless of whether the session actually did anything. Under opum-sdlc, a dirty tree needs a branch and a PR to land. Landing that PR ends a session, which fires the hook again, which writes another note and dirties the tree again. The loop is self-sustaining: no human or model input required to keep it going.

acceptanceCriteria.text: State the loop's actual trigger precisely: which of (a) the cursor rewrite (untracked/modified file every run) and (b) the tracker note (only when exactly one task is In Progress) is doing the dirtying in each observed case, since the fix differs depending on which one is load-bearing.

Design and ship a fix in opum-workflow's flush-state.sh (or the surrounding hook contract) that stops boilerplate-only commits/PRs from being generated, without losing the ability to reconstruct session state that the hook exists to provide -- see the design options opum-agent raised: skip the tracker note when nothing changed since the last note, or move it to the cursor (already the non-durable, discarded-on-read half of the handoff) instead of the tracker.

Confirm the fix does not reintroduce the original defect flush-state.sh was written to fix -- the lore-cli predecessor hook produced an EMPTY handover for a session that read, searched and reasoned without editing a file, because it derived state only from a PostToolUse checkpoint. A 'skip when nothing changed' rule must not silently drop a substantive but edit-free session the same way.
After the fix ships and at least one full session-end cycle has run against it, confirm no new boilerplate-only tracker-chore PR was opened, and that a real substantive note still lands durably.

plan: 1. AC1: read-only inspect .gitignore / git check-ignore in lore-web and opum-agent (siblings, no mutation) to isolate which half of the hook actually drives the loop.
2. AC2: design and implement a guard in hooks/flush-state.sh that withholds the tracker note when the repo has nothing uncommitted or unpushed, leaving the unconditional cursor write untouched.
3. AC3: verify by construction and by test that the cursor step (which alone fixed the lore-cli predecessor's empty-handover defect) is unaffected by the new guard.
4. Close the opum-marketplace-specific .gitignore gap the AC1 investigation surfaced, and wire hooks/test/run-tests.sh into CI, since nothing currently runs it despite the README's claim.
5. Extend hooks/test/run-tests.sh to lock in the new behavior, land via the normal branch/PR path.
implementationNotes: Filed by opum-agent (orchestrator), 2026-09-09, from evidence in lore-web: their last five commits (#71-#75) are ALL 'chore(tracker): commit session-renewal note', and LWEB-55 carries 12 implementation notes of which 9 are hook boilerplate, burying the 3 substantive ones -- so the cost is not PR noise, it is a task record whose signal is diluted to a quarter by its own tooling. opum-agent's own OPAG-64 shows the same pattern at smaller scale: 6 of its last 8 notes before 2026-09-09 were boilerplate.

Design framing from opum-agent, offered as a starting point rather than a ruling: the flush deliberately writes the tracker BEFORE the cursor because the tracker is the durable one (survives a discarded working tree / rebuilt machine) and the cursor is explicitly non-authoritative and discarded on read (see opum-handoff skill). This bug is a case of the durable channel being used to carry the least durable content -- a per-session heartbeat with no decision, reasoning, or handoff value on its own once the note is one of a run of identical ones.

INTERIM INSTRUCTION already given fleet-wide by opum-agent, in force until this ships: nobody opens a PR whose entire content is one of these boilerplate notes. Let it ride along uncommitted or bundled into the next substantive commit instead. This stops the loop without a code change while the fix is scheduled.

AC1 answered with read-only cross-repo evidence (git check-ignore / git log against lore-web and opum-agent's own working trees -- read-only, no HEAD/index/working-tree mutation performed on either sibling). Both already gitignore /.claude/handovers/ (per hooks/README.md's fleet-wide claim), so the cursor rewrite in step 2 dirties nothing in either repo -- git status never sees it. Yet both still produced the exact loop: lore-web's PRs #71-#75 and opum-agent's last eight OPAG-64 commits are almost entirely 'chore(tracker): ... session-renewal note'. That isolates the driver precisely: it is the tracker note (hooks/flush-state.sh step 1), not the cursor rewrite (step 2), that dirties .quest/ (committed, no gitignore available to it) on every SessionEnd/PreCompact and forces the branch+PR cycle. A second, repo-scoped finding from the same investigation: opum-marketplace itself does NOT gitignore /.claude/handovers/ (git check-ignore exit 1) -- it joined the fleet as the eighth repository and missed the convention hooks/README.md wrongly claimed was universal. So in this one repo, until fixed, BOTH mechanisms could contribute. lore-web's own commit d4744dc ('The opum-workflow write hook appends a note to whichever task is the sole In Progress one; here that's LWEB-55') independently confirms a second, related defect: the note lands on whichever task happens to be the sole In-Progress one, not necessarily the one the ending session actually worked on -- three of LWEB-55's nine boilerplate notes came from sessions working on unrelated tasks while LWEB-55 sat blocked. Recorded here as a follow-on finding, not fixed in this task: fixing it would mean session-scoping task attribution, which flush-state.sh cannot determine from git/tracker state alone, and is a materially different, riskier change than the one this task's ACs actually ask for.

AC2 shipped in hooks/flush-state.sh: step 1 now withholds the tracker note when DIRTY=0 and UNPUSHED is empty/0 -- i.e. only when the repository has an uncommitted file or an unpushed commit for the note to protect. Verified against the exact evidence from AC1: lore-web's boilerplate-only PRs each had a clean tree and no unpushed work at flush time (the note's own write was the sole diff), which is precisely the case this guard now withholds. The cursor step (step 2) is untouched and stays unconditional. Bundled two directly-related fixes surfaced by the same investigation rather than filing separate tasks for one-line, obviously-in-scope items: (a) opum-marketplace's .gitignore now ignores /.claude/handovers/, closing this repo's own eighth-repo gap so the guard isn't undermined here by a stray untracked cursor file counting toward DIRTY; (b) hooks/test/run-tests.sh is now wired into CI as 'check . hook tests' -- nothing ran it before despite the README's 'Run in CI on every push' claim, so this fix (and the whole hook contract) had zero CI enforcement.

AC3 verified two ways. By construction: the new guard sits entirely inside step 1's case statement and never touches step 2, which computes and writes the cursor unconditionally from the same live BRANCH/DIRTY/RECENT/ACTIVE variables regardless of the guard's outcome -- exactly the mechanism that already fully fixed the lore-cli predecessor's empty-handover defect (a PostToolUse-only checkpoint that stayed empty for an edit-free session), and that fix is untouched. By test: hooks/test/run-tests.sh's new 'a clean tree with nothing unpushed withholds the tracker note' case asserts the cursor is STILL written and STILL names the live task even when the tracker note is withheld. Also worth recording plainly: the withheld note never carried reasoning or decision content in the first place -- only branch name and file counts, both already live-derivable -- so withholding it on a clean, fully-pushed tree loses no information a restoring session could not already get from `git status`/`git log` and the live tracker. Full suite: 46/46 passing (up from 31; 15 new assertions across two new OMARK-23 cases plus fixes to an existing AC1 case whose sandbox implicitly relied on the pre-fix always-write behavior).

AC4 intentionally left open. It needs at least one full session-end cycle to run against the shipped fix, fleet-wide, before 'no new boilerplate-only PR was opened' can be asserted with evidence rather than faith -- checking it today would be exactly the kind of criterion-checked-on-faith the fleet's own quest-writes discipline warns against. Whoever next restores this task: confirm post-merge that (a) a repo whose sole In-Progress task ends a clean, fully-pushed session produces no new tracker-only PR, and (b) a session that does leave real uncommitted or unpushed work still gets a durable note. Then check AC4 and close the task.

Shipped. Merged as 7d7d5a0 (squash of PR #37, fix/OMARK-23-hook-tracker-note-loop). CI's 'check . manifests' job correctly caught that this changed opum-workflow's shipped hooks/ content with the version still at 0.4.0, and required either a version bump or a CHANGELOG.md Unreleased entry (OPAG-65's stacked-release guard). Chose the Unreleased entry over a bump: OMARK-21's observation week (2026-09-08 to 2026-09-15) is watching the currently-deployed 0.4.0 build, and a new release mid-week would force another fleet restart and reset that observation's baseline -- a call for the orchestrator to make deliberately, not a side effect of landing a bug fix. Left status In Progress rather than completing: AC4 (confirm post-ship, fleet-wide, that no new boilerplate-only PR appears and real notes still land) is explicitly not yet checkable with evidence and stays open until someone observes a real session-end cycle against the merged fix.

Interaction flagged by opum-agent, 2026-09-09: this task's own interim mitigation ('nobody opens a PR whose entire content is a hook-written note; let it ride along with the next substantive commit') trains a habit -- an uncommitted tracker change sitting in the working tree is normal and safe to leave for later -- that does not distinguish a hook-written note (designed to ride) from a deliberately authored tracker write like a completion (which will silently not exist if never committed). It caused a real incident: this session's own OMARK-26 completion sat uncommitted through OMARK-27's entire cycle. Filed as OMARK-28 (opum-sdlc: a deliberate tracker write gets its own PR, not a ride-along) rather than fixed here, since it is a documentation gap, not a hook bug -- but worth recording on THIS task because this task's own shipped fix (skip the note when nothing changed) partly retires the ambiguity at its source: fewer boilerplate notes riding along means fewer occasions for the habit to form in the first place. Neither fix makes the other unnecessary -- OMARK-28 documents the rule directly rather than relying on the mechanism alone to teach it.
